name: AI Transition Portfolio

benchmark.name: S&P 500 (SPY total return)
benchmark.note: Alpha is the portfolio's return minus SPY's, both from the same Monday open.

themes: AI power and grid (transition-themed, not ESG-screened)

constraints.note: Shocks are the owner-approved assumptions in the planning document, not forecasts.
constraints.capStatus: Modelled severe tail (-19.12%) is beyond the -18% limit by 1.12pp after D-005. On 12 Oct the owner decided to keep IREN at 4% and accepts the breach; the -18% limit is left unchanged and the breach stays on record. Claude recorded a dissent (3% at most until the contract is confirmed). The IREN shocks (-40% severe, -30% derating) were accepted by the owner on 12 Oct on condition they are evidence-backed. Evidence (Alpha Vantage weekly adjusted closes for IREN, Jun 2025 to 9 Oct 2026, retrieved 12 Oct): the worst 4-week fall was -43.9%, the worst 8-week fall -41.7%, and the deepest peak-to-trough on weekly closes was -47.1% (63.54 on 29 May to 33.62 on 17 Jul 2026), so the -40% severe and -30% derating shocks are not above what the stock has already done. Note the history is lighter than the worst case: at -47% the tail would be about -19.4%.

currencyPolicy: Developed-market positions (including IREN) hedged to sterling with rolling forwards; emerging-market names (TSM, LKOR, EWZ) unhedged; 14% sterling cash and Brazil reserve.

Real weaker than 5.2 per dollar
Copom does not cut in November

positions.name: IREN Limited
positions.thesis: Converting one of the larger power and data-centre pipelines in North America from bitcoin mining to AI cloud. FY26 (to 30 Jun): revenue $707.0m, with AI cloud $128.8m against $16.4m a year earlier and AI cloud ahead of mining in Q4 ($70.5m vs $66.7m); contracted annualised revenue of $4bn for 2026 capacity against $1bn operating, targeted live by 31 Dec; customer prepayments of 45-55% of GPU cost and GPU financing for most of the rest. An unconfirmed 11 Oct report says Anthropic signed a multiyear cloud deal (anonymous sources, no size, term or site). Balance sheet is the risk: about $7.6bn of debt, $6.3bn of convertible proceeds and $4.7bn of new equity in FY26, a $702.6m net loss including $638.8m of impairments, and non-investment-grade customers financed at 9%. Sized at 4% with a wide review level because the stock moves far more than the rest of the book.
thesisBreakers: IREN or Anthropic denies the report, or no contract is confirmed by the next company update
Contracted ARR target of $4bn by 31 Dec 2026 is cut or delayed
A convertible or equity raise that dilutes existing holders by more than 10%
A funding failure at a top AI lab
catalysts: Confirmation or denial of the Anthropic contract
Delivery of Microsoft Horizon 2 and Horizons 3-4 (Q4 2026 target)

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: Hedge for a geopolitical shock (Brent near $105 on the Iran conflict); weak when real yields rise, so sized at 6% and not relied on alone.
thesisBreakers: Real yields rising sharply while geopolitical risk fades

cash.name: Brazil runoff reserve (cash)
cash.role: Dry powder; deploy after 25 Oct runoff

entryPlan: Enter at Monday's open. Buy only half of TSM, NVDA and LKOR then; the other half after TSMC results on Thu 15 Oct. EWZ staged; IREN: a first tranche of 2% of NAV (GBP 2,000, about 75 shares at the $35.19 reference and a GBP/USD rate of about 1.32) bought at Monday's open price, sized in pounds not shares; if the open is more than 10% above the reference ($38.71) nothing is bought at the open and the day is reviewed instead; the other 2% only once IREN or Anthropic confirms the contract and IREN's own breakers have not fired, and counted as the same change as the TSM/NVDA/LKOR second halves if confirmed by 15 Oct, otherwise bought no earlier than the next week's change allowance (decision D-005); 7% Brazil reserve decided after the 25 Oct runoff. Each second half is bought only if that holding's own named thesis breakers (see its entry) and the portfolio-wide triggers have not fired by then; TSM's include a gross-margin guide below 65-67% or a material capex cut at TSMC's results. For any holding whose breaker has fired, the tranche stays in bills and the day is an ACT decision.
reserveRule: If Bolsonaro wins on 25 Oct and the real holds near 5.0, add up to 5% EWZ. If Lula wins, stay at 5% unless the review level is hit and keep the reserve in bills. Any deployment must first re-run the severe-tail test and stay inside the -18% cap: EWZ at -12% adds about -0.12pp per 1% of NAV, so the extra EWZ must be funded by an equal cut elsewhere (or by showing the cap still holds), and the check is logged in the decision.

verdicts.WATCH: Something moved; named and monitored, no trade.
verdicts.ACT: A trade is proposed. Only on the conditions in actRules.

actRules: A position's review level or a drawdown step is hit
A trade scheduled in entryPlan (initial construction and its conditional second tranche)

drawdownLadder.action: Review every thesis; cut GOOGL and NEE first.
Cut TSM, NVDA and LKOR by a third, convert any undeployed Brazil reserve to T-bills, then sell the remaining equity pro rata until T-bills are 25% of NAV.
Move everything to cash and reset.

Amundi Korea fund: tracks a 20/35 capped MSCI Korea index, synthetic swap; reference price is the owner's broker NAV (EUR 181.23, 11 Oct) versus a Xetra close of EUR 178.34 on 9 Oct, and the EUR/USD effect on this row not modelled

IREN: the Anthropic contract is an unconfirmed report from anonymous sources (The Information via AI Weekly, 11 Oct); the severe-tail shock for IREN (-40%) is Claude's assumption, accepted by the owner on 12 Oct on condition it is evidence-backed (weekly closes show a worst 4-week fall of -43.9% and a peak-to-trough of -47.1%); IREN's Friday close ($35.19) predates the weekend news, so Monday's open may gap

scenarios.method: Portfolio effect (% of NAV) = sum over positions of weightPct x shock% / 100. Cash and the Brazil reserve are held at zero return. Shocks are USD price moves; sterling/FX effects and hedge costs are NOT in these figures; see fxSensitivity.

allTargets.inputs: unrounded targetUSD / refPriceUSD - 1 for each position (the targetPct field is that value rounded to 0.1)

allReviewLevels.inputs: unrounded reviewLevelUSD / refPriceUSD - 1 for each position (the reviewPct field is that value rounded to 0.1)

scenarios.note: Shock sizes are the owner-approved assumptions in the planning document, not forecasts. Exception: the IREN shocks (-40% severe, -30% derating) are Claude's assumptions (D-005), accepted by the owner on 12 Oct as evidence-backed: IREN's worst 4-week fall was -43.9% and its deepest peak-to-trough -47.1% (weekly closes, Jun 2025 to Oct 2026).

fxSensitivity.note: The -18% cap is tested on USD price shocks only. A concurrent 1% sterling rise on the unhedged sleeve takes the severe tail to about -19.30%. D-002 (11 Oct) accepted the cap as a price-only limit with 28% unhedged; D-005 (12 Oct) replaces Itau with a hedged IREN, so the unhedged sleeve is now 25%.

ladderRule: A drawdown-ladder action is one change for the weekly limit and is exempt from maxChangesPerWeek; it takes precedence over it.
ladderBasis: atPct is controlling and is measured from the running NAV peak (status.json drawdownFromPeakPct). navGBP is only the illustrative level while the peak is the 100,000 starting capital.
entryChangeRule: Initial construction on 12 Oct counts as one change, and the conditional second tranche after TSMC's results counts as one change; the conditional second IREN tranche is part of that same change if confirmed by Thu 15 Oct, otherwise it is a single change in a later week and is never a third change in the same week. Ladder actions stay exempt under ladderRule.
